TCGA PRAD Pathogenic/Oncogenic Mutation Analysis & Gene-T Stage Association
============================================================================

1. TOP PATHOGENIC/ONCOGENIC MUTATED GENES
------------------------------------------

Filtering: Non-synonymous mutations only (Missense, Nonsense, Frame Shift, Splice Site, In Frame, Translation Start, Nonstop) in COSMIC Cancer Gene Census (CGC) genes. CGC was used because the MAF lacks per-variant ONCOGENIC/CLIN_SIG columns.

Top 10 pathogenic mutated genes (of 339 samples with CGC mutations):

  TP53    61 samples (18.0%) — predominantly missense; known PRAD driver
  ATM     22 samples (6.5%) — mostly missense; DNA damage repair
  PTEN    17 samples (5.0%) — mix of truncating and missense; tumor suppressor
  PIK3CA  14 samples (4.1%) — all missense (hotspot); oncogene
  KDM6A   13 samples (3.8%) — histone demethylase; mixed types
  CTNNB1  13 samples (3.8%) — all missense (beta-catenin hotspot)
  NOTCH2  11 samples (3.2%) — mostly frameshift; tumor suppressor
  SETD2   10 samples (2.9%) — histone methyltransferase
  APC     10 samples (2.9%) — mostly nonsense; Wnt pathway suppressor
  BRCA2    9 samples (2.7%) — DNA repair; clinical significance

Notable: SPOP (11.4%) and FOXA1 (5.6%) are top mutated genes in the unfiltered landscape but absent from the CGC census. They are well-established PRAD drivers; their absence is a limitation of the CGC pan-cancer gene list.

2. VISUALIZATION
-----------------

Six figures generated in outputs/figures/:
  fig1a_top_pathogenic_genes.pdf — Bar chart of top 20 CGC pathogenic genes
  fig1b_oncoplot.pdf — Oncoplot heatmap (binary mutation matrix, 80 samples × 20 genes)
  fig1c_mutation_types.pdf — Mutation type distribution for top 10 genes
  fig2a_expr_tstage_volcano.pdf — Genome-wide expression vs T stage volcano plot
  fig2b_mutation_tstage_bars.pdf — Mutation status vs T stage bar charts

3. GENE-T STAGE ASSOCIATION
-----------------------------

A. Mutation status vs T stage (Fisher's exact, BH-FDR across 20 genes):

  TP53: OR=3.08, p=0.0006, FDR=0.012 — SIGNIFICANT
    TP53-mutated tumors: 16.1% at T3+ vs 5.9% at T2
    (TP53 mutation is enriched in extraprostatic/advanced disease)

  ATM: OR=2.89, FDR=0.436 — trend only
  KDM6A: OR=0.26, FDR=0.381 — depleted in T3+ (not significant)
  PTEN, PIK3CA, CTNNB1: no significant association

B. Gene expression vs T stage (Spearman, genome-wide, 490 patients):

  5,479 genes at FDR < 0.05 (26.7% of all tested genes)

  Top positive (higher expression = advanced T stage):
    ASPN  (rho=+0.39) — asporin, ECM remodeling
    CCNE2 (rho=+0.35) — cyclin E2, cell cycle
    CCNA2 (rho=+0.35) — cyclin A2, cell cycle
    CENPA (rho=+0.35) — centromere protein, mitosis
    FAP   (rho=+0.34) — fibroblast activation protein, stroma

  Top negative (higher expression = early T stage):
    KCNK6  (rho=-0.38) — potassium channel, differentiated tissue
    EPHX2  (rho=-0.38) — epoxide hydrolase, normal prostate
    CHRNA2 (rho=-0.37) — nicotinic receptor, differentiated tissue
    AZGP1  (rho=-0.33) — androgen-regulated, differentiation marker
    CD38   (rho=-0.33) — cyclic ADP ribose hydrolase

  Interpretation: Advanced T stage is associated with upregulation of cell-cycle
  and ECM-remodeling genes, and downregulation of differentiated prostate tissue
  markers — consistent with dedifferentiation and invasive biology.

OUTPUT FILES:

  outputs/figures/fig1b_oncoplot.pdf
  outputs/figures/fig1c_mutation_types.pdf
  outputs/figures/fig2a_expr_tstage_volcano.pdf
  outputs/figures/fig2b_mutation_tstage_bars.pdf
  outputs/mutation_tstage_fisher.csv
  outputs/gene_tstage_spearman.csv

## Routing Decision

I selected **`tabular_genomics_analyst`** because the task asks for somatic mutation frequency/landscape analysis (MAF table), pathogenic/oncogenic filtering, and statistical association between mutation status and clinical T stage — all table-level genomic analysis, not expression matrix modeling.

## Summary of Results

**Top 10 Pathogenic/Oncogenic Mutated Genes (COSMIC Cancer Gene Census filtered):**

| Gene | Mutated Samples | Frequency |
|------|----------------|-----------|
| TP53 | 61 | 18.0% |
| ATM | 22 | 6.5% |
| PTEN | 17 | 5.0% |
| PIK3CA | 14 | 4.1% |
| KDM6A | 13 | 3.8% |
| CTNNB1 | 13 | 3.8% |
| NOTCH2 | 11 | 3.2% |
| SETD2 | 10 | 2.9% |
| APC | 10 | 2.9% |
| BRCA2 | 9 | 2.7% |

Note: SPOP (11.4%) and FOXA1 (5.6%) are top PRAD-specific drivers but absent from the CGC pan-cancer census.

**Gene–T Stage Association:**
- **TP53 mutation** is significantly enriched in advanced T3+ disease (OR = 3.08, FDR = 0.012): 16.1% of T3+ tumors carry TP53 mutations vs. 5.9% of T2 tumors.
- At the expression level, 5,479 genes (26.7%) significantly correlate with T stage (FDR < 0.05), with cell-cycle/proliferation genes (ASPN, CCNE2, CCNA2, CENPA) positively associated and differentiated prostate markers (KCNK6, EPHX2, AZGP1, CD38) negatively associated.

**Visualizations:** 5 figures (oncoplot, mutation landscape heatmap, mutation type breakdown, volcano plot for expression vs. T stage, grouped bars for mutation–T stage) generated as PNG + SVG + PDF in `outputs/figures/`.

criterion_2.reason: Clearly defines a proxy rule using non-silent variants and CGC gene membership, covering the required filter logic.

criterion_4.reason: Extracts PATH_T_STAGE, handles missing data, simplifies stages, and uses T2 vs T3/T4 for the main test.

criterion_5.reason: Applies Fisher's exact test with BH-FDR correction to 2x2 tables, and all tested genes meet the implicit minimum mutation count.

criterion_6.reason: Correctly reports TP53 as the only FDR-significant gene but misses the exact FDR anchor and does not test CLIN_T_STAGE.
